newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close higher on local funds buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close higher on local funds buying.

text.p: Indian shares recorded smart gains at major bourses on Thursday helped by fresh purchases from local funds and short-covering by punters, dealers said.
"Everything was heavily oversold and some correction had to come. Some buying from Indian institutions helped to prop up sentiment," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) jumped 88.71 points or 2.92 percent by close, a shade off 3,129.69, the day's highest level.
Traders said hectic short-covering by Calcutta and Bombay punters combined with bids by local funds pushed up prices.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 23.7 points or 2.7 percent to end at 898.42.
Traders said foreign funds were select buyers in HDFC, MTNL, BSES, Wartsila Diesel, Bajaj Auto, Hindustan Lever, TELCO, Infosys and BPCL.

Software firm Infosys Technologies on Thursday reported a 76 percent rise in its 1996/97 (April-March) first half net profit to 141.1 million rupees. The stock was up 36.0 rupees to 685 rupees at the BSE on Thursday with 1,000 shares traded.
The CRISIL 500-stock index advanced 17.52 points to 604.98.
Analysts said the market rise was unlikely to sustain.
"The political risk factor is the major constraint for the market today. All the other factors are functions of the political situation," said Anthony Duckworth, director of research at W.I Carr.

Meanwhile, latest results from state assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state showed the nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party leading in a triangular race, but falling short of its goal of winning an absolute majority.
Out of 376 of 425 results declared in the state assembly, the BJP had won 158. In the last state election in 1993, the BJP won 176 seats.
